How to Sell Stocks (NSE, FYERS app)

On this page

  1. 1. Two kinds of selling
  2. 2. Steps in the FYERS app (selling shares you own)
  3. 3. Demat authorisation (needed only for delivery sells)
  4. 4. After the sale
  5. 5. Common mistakes

Written Oct 2026. Exact button names in the FYERS app may change; the steps stay the same. Education, not investment advice. Costs of a sale: see breakeven_move_fyers.md.

1. Two kinds of selling

You want toProduct typeRule
Sell shares you own (in your demat, i.e. Holdings)CNC / DeliveryAny day, any time the market is open. Needs demat authorisation (section 3).
Close an intraday buy made todayIntraday (MIS)Sell before the broker's auto square-off (~3:15–3:20 pm); otherwise the broker closes it for you (with a fee).
Sell first without owning (short) and buy back laterIntraday (MIS) onlyMust buy back the same day. Holding a short overnight in cash stocks is not allowed; that needs futures.

2. Steps in the FYERS app (selling shares you own)

  1. Portfolio → Holdings → tap the stock.
  2. Tap Exit / Sell.
  3. Product: CNC / Delivery (for shares in your demat).
  4. Quantity: all shares or part of them.
  5. Order type:
    • Market: sells now at the best available price. Fast, but you take whatever price is there (slippage).
    • Limit: sells only at your price or better, e.g. "sell 10 at ₹4,020". May not fill.
    • Stop-loss (SL / SL-M): waits until price falls to a trigger, then sells. Used to cap a loss.
    • GTT (good till triggered): a stop or target that stays active for months; useful for swing trades.
  6. Swipe / confirm Sell.
  7. Authorise if asked (section 3).
  8. Check Orders: "Executed / Complete" = sold. "Pending / Open" = waiting at your limit price.

Market hours: pre-open 9:00–9:08 am, normal trading 9:15 am–3:30 pm, Monday–Friday (not exchange holidays). AMO (after-market order): place it in the evening; it goes to the exchange next morning.

3. Demat authorisation (needed only for delivery sells)

Shares leave your demat account when you sell, so SEBI requires your permission:

  • DDPI (one-time): sign it once (online with Aadhaar e-sign); after that, sells go through without extra steps. Easiest.
  • eDIS / CDSL TPIN: without DDPI, before selling you enter your CDSL TPIN + OTP to approve those shares. Done once per day per stock.

If you skip this, the sell order is rejected.

4. After the sale

  • Settlement is T+1: the money is settled the next working day. You can usually use the sale amount to buy other shares the same day, but you can withdraw it to your bank only after settlement.
  • Charges: STT, brokerage, exchange/SEBI fees, GST, stamp duty (on buys) and a DP charge (~₹14.75) per stock per sell day on delivery sells. Shown in the contract note emailed that evening.
  • Tax: held under 1 year → short-term gain taxed at 20%; 1 year or more → 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year. Intraday profit is business income at your slab rate. Losses can be set off against gains; keep the contract notes.
  • Which shares count as sold: first in, first out (the oldest shares you bought are treated as sold first) — affects tax.

5. Common mistakes

  • Choosing Intraday product for shares you own → order rejected or treated wrongly; use CNC / Delivery.
  • BTST (selling shares bought yesterday, before they reach your demat): allowed, but if the seller who sold them to you fails to deliver, you get "short delivery" and an auction penalty. Rare, but possible.
  • A market order in a thinly traded stock can fill far below the last price; use a limit order there.
  • Forgetting to close an intraday position → auto square-off at a bad price + extra fee.
